correctness.rationale: The projective orbit map G->H·[eta] has uniform fibers of cardinality |G|/m(eta). For nonzero f in C^2, the coefficient vanishes exactly when [pi(g)eta] is the single ray [f-perp], so the zero set is empty or one whole fiber; varying f realizes every orbit ray and proves p0(pi,eta)=1/m(eta). The quotient H acts faithfully on CP^1, and each nonidentity projective unitary fixes at most two rays, so a ray outside the finite union of fixed sets has trivial stabilizer and orbit size |H|, yielding the global minimum. The sharp sample threshold follows because no nonzero coefficient can vanish on more than |G|/m points and one can attain exactly that fiber.

originality.rationale: Führ--Oussa already define the zero-proportion invariant, prove its invariance under quotienting by the projective kernel, state the sharp uniform-sampling consequence, and give the exact full-spark formula p0=(d-1)/|G|. In complex dimension two, a generic ray for the faithful projective quotient has trivial stabilizer because each nonidentity projective unitary fixes only finitely many rays; its orbit is therefore a set of |H| distinct rays, which is automatically full spark in C^2. This mechanically gives the submitted minimized value p0(pi)=1/|H|. For a fixed window, the remaining formula p0(pi,eta)=1/m(eta) is the immediate orbit--stabilizer evaluation of the source definition because f-perp is one projective ray. The claimed sampling threshold is then exactly the source's sampling observation. The package is mathematically correct, but the final claim is a routine dimension-two specialization of the published framework rather than an independent theorem.

final_claim: For a two-dimensional unitary representation of a finite group, the maximal matrix-coefficient zero proportion for a window eta is the reciprocal of its projective orbit size m(eta); minimizing over windows gives p0(pi)=1/|G/K|=|K|/|G| with minimizers exactly the trivial-stabilizer rays, and the universal sample-count threshold is |G|/m(eta).
